sec: When to biopsy vs dialyse first · p779

items.q: A patient with RPGN has a very high serum creatinine. The book advises against immediate renal biopsy because:
opts: It will not show crescents at this stage
The kidney is too small for a safe puncture
Immunofluorescence cannot be performed at high creatinine
items.exp: Note: biopsy should not be done if serum creatinine is markedly increased, as it may cause uremic bleeding. (Book p779)

items.q: Arrange the correct sequence when the serum creatinine is very high — 1) First step  2) Then  3) If the value decreases … A) Recheck serum creatinine  B) Dialysis  C) Biopsy
items.exp: When the creatinine is very high: first step dialysis → recheck serum creatinine → if the value decreases, proceed to biopsy. (Book p779)

items.q: In the high-creatinine RPGN algorithm, biopsy is performed:
opts: After dialysis, provided the rechecked serum creatinine decreases
Only when the creatinine exceeds 5.5 mg/dL
Simultaneously with the first dialysis session
items.exp: Algorithm: dialysis → recheck creatinine → biopsy if the value decreases (avoiding uremic bleeding from an immediate biopsy). (Book p779)

items.q: According to the page, an immediately raised serum creatinine is an absolute contraindication to ever performing a renal biopsy.
opts: False — dialysis is done first and biopsy follows once the creatinine falls
True — biopsy is never repeated in such patients
True — biopsy then has to be replaced by CT imaging
False — biopsy is performed before dialysis instead
items.exp: It is the immediate biopsy that is avoided (uremic bleeding risk); after dialysis, if the creatinine decreases, biopsy is performed. (Book p779)
